summary: Parallel-line angle bisectors and resulting quadrilateral
derivation: At P, the two angles APQ and BPQ form a straight angle, so their bisectors are perpendicular; likewise at Q, CQP and PQD are supplementary so their bisectors are perpendicular. As APB and CQD are parallel the complementary bisector intersections give a four-right-angle quadrilateral.

summary: Angle relation across parallel families
Angle-bisector and circle-diameter cyclic claims
answer: Statement I true; Statement II true
derivation: For intersections of successive interior-angle bisectors of a quadrilateral, each opposite angle pair of the formed quadrilateral sums to 360 degrees minus half the sum of the original four angles, which is 180 degrees; hence cyclic (Statement I). In ABCD, angle ABC=180-140=40 degrees, angle ACB=90 degrees since AB is a diameter, so angle BAC=50 degrees (Statement II). Choice C.
check: The original interior angles total 360 degrees, yielding supplementary opposite angles in the bisector quadrilateral. For ABC triangle, 40+90+50=180 degrees, so the second inferred angle also checks.

summary: Chord-distance relation and cyclic quadrilateral claims
derivation: Statement I: chord length 6 at perpendicular distance 4 has half-chord 3, so radius²=3²+4²=25. For chord length 8, half-chord 4 and distance √(25−4²)=3, true. Statement II: the outer circle makes A,B,C,D concyclic, hence ∠CDA=∠CBA (same chord CA). The inner circle makes A,B,E,F concyclic, so ∠FEA=∠FBA (same chord FA). Because B,F,C are collinear and A,E,D are collinear as shown, the angles agree, implying EF∥DC. Thus both are true; printed option A.
check: By directed-angle chasing, angle(CD,DA)=angle(CB,BA)=angle(FB,BA)=angle(FE,EA); since DA and EA lie on the same straight line, CD is parallel to FE. This independently checks the inner/outer cyclic-circle figure claim.

summary: Intercept of a linear graph at x=0
derivation: A point on the y-axis has x=0. Substitution in 4x+y=12 yields 4×0+y=12, so the y-intercept is (0,12), option D.
check: The point (0,12) satisfies 4×0+12=12 and has zero abscissa, confirming that it lies on the y-axis.

summary: Coordinate reflection, distance and quadrant sign
derivation: Reflection of (7,5) across the y-axis reverses only x to (-7,5). The point (3,4) lies sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 units from the origin. In quadrant III, distances 3 from x-axis and 6 from y-axis require y=-3 and x=-6, giving (-6,-3), printed option C.
check: Absolute ordinate 3 gives distance to x-axis 3, absolute abscissa 6 gives distance to y-axis 6, both coordinates negative as required in quadrant III.

summary: Abscissa/ordinate identification
derivation: The abscissa of A(10,5) is 10. The ordinate of B(-7,-4) is -4. Taking the stipulated difference gives 10-(-4)=14, printed option A.
check: Projection to the x-coordinate of A gives 10, while projection to the y-coordinate of B gives -4; subtracting a negative adds 4.

summary: Coordinate transformations and sign reversals
derivation: For ordinate −4, abscissa two more than three times the ordinate is 2+3(−4)=−10. Sign reversal sends (5,−4) to (−5,4), so coordinatewise sum gives (0,0). Reflection across the x-axis sends (4,9) to (4,−9). Original printed option B.
check: The computed first coordinate obeys x=3y+2 at y=−4; the original and negated point sum to the origin, while x-axis reflection leaves the abscissa unchanged.

summary: Uniqueness of a parallel line through a point
derivation: In Euclidean geometry Playfair's equivalent to the parallel postulate says that through a point b not on an existing line a exactly one line can be drawn parallel to a. This selects option B.
check: Existence and uniqueness both matter: zero would contradict existence; two or infinitely many violate the Euclidean uniqueness statement.

summary: Identify Euclid’s postulate and distinguish axioms
answer: Euclid third postulate: arbitrary centre and radius circle
derivation: Euclid's third postulate licenses drawing a circle with any centre and radius, which is choice A. Extending a terminated line is postulate two; all right angles equal is postulate four; whole>part is a common notion.
check: Distinguishing the other distractors by their numbering and axiom/postulate status uniquely selects A.

summary: Equality preserved by adding equal lengths
answer: equals added to equals remain equal
derivation: With ordered collinear points P,Q,R,S, PR=PQ+QR and QS=QR+RS; since PQ=RS, these sums are equal.
check: Replacing PQ with RS in PR yields QR+RS=QS. This works for every ordered placement P-Q-R-S.

summary: Fixed cost plus a variable rate
derivation: Write total milk expenditure as a fixed INR 700 plus INR 25 for each of x extra litres: y=700+25x. Rearranging yields -25x+y=700, printed option A.
check: At zero extra litres, expenditure equals 700. At two extra litres, y=750 and -25 times 2 plus 750 still equals 700.

summary: Infer coefficients from a known solution
derivation: Substitute x=y=1 into the first printed equation, obtaining 9p+12p=63 and hence p=3. The second gives 5+2q=3q, so q=5; choice A.
check: Check 9×3+12×3=63 and 5+2×5=15=3×5. Both original constraints hold. This simultaneously checks the first and second equation at the claimed point.

check: Algebra checked against printed givens and choices; no official key receipt.

summary: Two linked age constraints
derivation: Let the son's present age be s, so the father's is 60-s. Six years ago father 54-s and son s-6, with 54-s=5(s-6). Thus 84=6s and s=14; after six years the son is 20. Printed option A.

summary: Income/expenditure ratio and savings constraints
derivation: Let incomes of P and Q be 5x and 4x, and expenditures 3y and 2y. Equal savings ₹1600 impose 5x−3y=1600 and 4x−2y=1600. Multiply the second by 3 and first by 2, subtract to obtain 2x=1600 and x=800. P's income is 5×800=₹4000, option C.

summary: Spatial reasoning from dice orientations
derivation: Faces 2,4,6,1 each occur adjacent to the same face 5 in the two inspected dice views, leaving face 3 opposite 5. Mapping the three source views as consistent quarter-turns fixes the unknown second front face as 4; printed choice B.

summary: Factor cubic volume into dimensions
derivation: The given volume polynomial is x³+x²−12x. Factor out x to obtain x(x²+x−12). Since 4 and −3 multiply to −12 and sum to 1, this becomes x(x+4)(x−3), printed option B.

summary: Polynomial divisibility under two linear factors
derivation: Money polynomial P(x)=x^3+2ax+b is divisible by x-1 and x+1. Thus P(1)=0 and P(-1)=0; solving 1+2a+b=0 and -1-2a+b=0 gives a=-1/2,b=0; P(4)=4^3-4=60.
check: P(x)=x(x-1)(x+1), so P(4)=4*3*5=60. This factor form has zeros at x=1 and x=-1 as required.

summary: Complementary probability from categorical survey
derivation: Of 400 surveyed, 250 work in government offices, leaving 150 in the private sector. Under equally likely selection from the survey, P(private)=150/400=3/8, printed choice B.
check: Private probability 3/8 plus government 5/8 is 1; integer count 400×3/8=150.

summary: Colour draws with equally likely objects
derivation: A bag containing three red, five black and four white balls has twelve equally likely choices. The five favourable black balls yield probability 5/12, printed option C.
check: P(red)+P(black)+P(white)=3/12+5/12+4/12=1, verifying the sample-space partition. The favourable count is strictly between zero and the full set of 12 outcomes.

summary: Two-dice event counting
derivation: Two independent six-sided dice have 36 equiprobable ordered outcomes. Sums greater than nine are 10 (3 ways), 11 (2 ways), 12 (1 way): 6 favorable outcomes, giving 6/36=1/6, option C.
check: Explicit ordered pairs: (4,6),(5,5),(6,4),(5,6),(6,5),(6,6), six outcomes out of 36.

summary: Complement of prime-labelled cards
derivation: There are 50 distinct integers from 51 through 100 inclusive. Exactly ten are prime (53,59,61,67,71,73,79,83,89,97); the other 40 are not prime. Thus probability =40/50=4/5, printed D.
check: The ten primes are all >50 and <=100, so the complement is 1−10/50=40/50; prime and nonprime probabilities sum to one.

summary: Reverse compound-interest principal
derivation: The annual compound-interest rate 16 2/3 percent is 1/6, giving a 2-year multiplier (7/6)^2=49/36. Borrowed principal equals the repaid total 20825 times 36/49, which is INR 15300, option A.
check: 15300 multiplied by 49/36 equals 20825 exactly, verifying that the final amount under annual compounding matches the given repayment.

summary: Combine two constant work rates
derivation: A completes 1/9 of the work per day and B completes 1/12 of the work per day. Their joint rate is 1/9+1/12=7/36 per day; completion time is 36/7 days, or 5 1/7 days, printed option A.
check: Multiplying 36/7 days by their combined 7/36 work per day yields exactly one complete job. Thus the combined daily rate and duration are mutually inverse, as physically required.

summary: Conditional population percentage calculation
derivation: Men comprise 40 percent and 75 percent of these earn above the threshold, so 30 percent of all employees are high-earning men. Overall 45 percent are high earners; high-earning women are 15 percent of total, or 15/60=1/4 of women. Therefore 3/4 of women are not above threshold, choice D.
check: Split a population of 100 into 40 men and 60 women: 30 high-earning men, 15 high-earning women, and 45 lower-earning women. The sought fraction is 45/60=3/4.

summary: Relative speed of approaching trains
derivation: Trains approaching on parallel tracks have relative speed 54+36=90 km per hour, equivalent to 25 m per second. To clear each other after first meeting, combined lengths 150+175=325 metres must pass; 325/25=13 seconds, printed option B.
check: In 13 seconds the combined relative displacement is 13 times 25=325 m, exactly the total train lengths.

summary: Recover principal from amount and interest
derivation: The annual simple interest is 16 percent. Over one year and three months the period is 5/4 years, and accumulated interest equals 0.16*1.25=0.20 of the principal. Hence total 12000 is 1.20 of principal; principal 10000, printed option B.
check: Interest on INR 10000 for 5/4 year at 16 percent per year is INR 2000; amount INR 12000 as required.

summary: Relate past and future age ratios
derivation: Let one-year-ago ages of Gaurav and Sachin be 6k and 7k. Four years from now they are 6k+5 and 7k+5; their ratio 7:8 implies 8(6k+5)=7(7k+5), giving k=5. Sachin's current age is 7*5+1=36 years, printed option D.
check: Ages now are 31 and 36. One year ago 30:35=6:7; four years hence 35:40=7:8, confirming both ratio conditions.

summary: Solve rate equal to time under simple interest
derivation: Simple interest as a fraction of principal is rt/100. With interest=P/9 and the numerical rate equal to the term, r=t, so r²/100=1/9. Positive r=10/3 percent, option A.
check: At r=t=10/3, rt/100=(100/9)/100=1/9; the chosen annual rate is positive.

summary: Solve mixed worker productivity rates
derivation: Let a man complete m jobs/day and a boy b jobs/day. Source gives 6m+8b=1/10 and 26m+48b=1/2; subtracting appropriate multiples yields m=1/100 and b=1/200. Therefore 15 men and 20 boys do 15/100+20/200=1/4 job/day, completing one job in four days, printed option A.
check: Source conditions hold: 6/100+8/200=1/10 job/day, 26/100+48/200=1/2 job/day. New group works 1/4 job/day and finishes in 4 days.
